Definition: from κοῦφος (light in weight); to unload:--lighten.
BiblicalUsage: Acts 27:38 is the word's only appearance, in the middle of the storm: after eating, the sailors lightened the ship by throwing the wheat into the sea. It is a plain, practical word for unloading weight to save the vessel.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it as given that there is a small lesson here I keep coming back to: sometimes survival means letting go of the cargo, and the cargo is not always worth the ship.
